guards.what: G2 (LIVE, mechanism owned by relic/paels_eye G3): the hook never fires on a Pael's Eye extra turn
guards.rationale: The recorded divergence was that CombatState.end_turn consulted should_take_extra_turn FIRST and returned, skipping on_player_turn_end, the turn-end cards, the flush AND after_player_turn_end. Today sts2_rl/combat.py:793-809 runs all four unconditionally and the extra-turn test has moved to :823, with the comment at :816-822 recording the old trace. That is CombatManager.cs's order exactly — Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (:1179), DoTurnEnd (:1191), FlushPlayerHand (:1296), Hook.AfterTurnEnd (:1307), then ShouldTakeExtraTurn (:1366). So relics/parrying_shield.py:24-39 now deals its 6 damage and takes its CombatTargets draw on a Pael's-Eye turn, matching ParryingShield.cs's AfterSideTurnEnd.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: MECHANISM: the sim's CombatState.end_turn consults should_take_extra_turn FIRST and `return`s (combat.py:648-652), skipping on_player_turn_end, the turn-end cards, the hand flush AND after_player_turn_end (combat.py:654-665). C# runs the entire turn-end pass and only then asks (Hook.AfterTurnEnd at CombatManager.cs:1307 vs Hook.ShouldTakeExtraTurn at :1366). So a turn in which Pael's Eye grants an extra turn loses Parrying Shield's 6 damage entirely, and loses the CombatTargets draw with it. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b11.py eye-turnend`: a sentinel listener records after_player_turn_end firing without Pael's Eye and not firing with it, on the same end_turn call). Both sides ported and co-obtainable: Parrying Shield is Uncommon in the grab bag, Pael's Eye is Ancient from the ported Pael shrine, and the turn Pael's Eye triggers is by definition one where no card was played -- which is a turn the player is likely to be holding block from a previous Defend. Per binding rule 3 this is ONE mechanism with ONE verdict, recorded in full at audit/records/relic/paels_eye.json guard G3 (which owns the extra-turn machinery); reproduced here because the lost 6 damage is this relic's observable.

Structurally satisfied: after_player_turn_end is fired only from the player's own end_turn path (combat.py:665) with the combat's single player, so the owner is always a participant. Multiplayer-only in effect, noted per the shared contract rather than verdicted as a divergence.

guards.what: N2: `if (creature != null)` (ParryingShield.cs:29-33) -- C# tolerates NextItem returning null on an empty list; the sim returns early on an empty candidate list
guards.rationale: parrying_shield.py:30-31 (`if not living: return`) reaches the same outcome and, importantly, does so BEFORE touching the RNG -- which matters for parity because C#'s NextItem on an empty collection returns null without consuming a draw. Checked deliberately: a port that drew first and then bailed would desynchronise the CombatTargets stream on any turn that ends with no living enemies.

guards.what: N3: the sim adds a `_check_win()` after the damage (parrying_shield.py:38); C# has no such call in the relic
guards.rationale: Not an addition to behaviour but the sim's stand-in for the CheckWinCondition that follows the game's own commands -- Relic._check_win's docstring says exactly that (relics/base.py:299-304), and CombatManager runs CheckWinCondition around the turn-end hooks (CombatManager.cs:1181, :1208). Without it a relic that lands the killing blow at turn end would hand back a turn with no living enemies. Same shape and same verdict as the other turn-end damage relics.
